newsitem.title: USA: Housing bond issuers pleased with Senate HUD bill.
newsitem.headline: Housing bond issuers pleased with Senate HUD bill.

text.p: A spokesman for issuers of state housing bonds said localities are pleased with the fiscal year 1997 funding bill cleared by the U.S. Senate late Thursday for HUD and other agencies.

"Wonderful" is the way Barbara Thompson, director of government affairs for the National Council of State Housing Agencies, described bill provisions for renewal of contracts due to expire next year under the Section 8 rent subsidy program.

"For any property with a mortgage financed or insured by a public entity, including a state housing finance agency, that contract will be continued for that year at its current rent level," Thompson said.
"It basically carves out that class of properties and allows those contracts to be continued at their current rent," Thompson said.
If a property has a rent up to 120 percent of fair market rent, it will be continued at that level, she said.

However, a site with a rent over 120 percent has two options, she said. The property owner can accept a contract at 120 percent or participate in a HUD demonstration project that calls for mortgage "reengineering," she said.
Under reengineering, rent support would be reduced, she said.
The HUD funding bill now goes before House and Senate negotiators to work out differences in the chambers' bills.

Undisputed are spending levels for HUD's Community Development Block Grant program, which would get roughly $4.6 billion in both bills, and for the HOME investment partnerships program, which would get $1.4 billion.
Conferees are expected to meet next week.
